clue.text: Aggressive person with work as door-to door salesman

definitions.meaning: a warmonger or hardliner, the opposite of a dove
to peddle goods by going from house to house

explanation.surface: A pushy salesman goes from house to house.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a hardliner is called a hawk, and to hawk wares is to peddle them on the doorstep.

clue.text: Affected mountaineer's temporary sleeping quarters?

definitions.meaning: exaggeratedly theatrical or mannered in style
a climbers' base set up high on a mountain

explanation.definitionFit: High camp is extravagant affected style, and literally a camp pitched high up a mountain.

clue.text: Word for nondescript articles that's now inaccurate

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are set down inaccurately, i.e. jumbled

explanation.surface: A term for odds and ends that is no longer correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatnots is a vague word for miscellaneous small items one cannot name.

clue.text: Policeman's introduced extra measure for secure accommodation

indicators.note: something is introduced into the policeman's abbreviation, so it goes inside

parts.note: PC is police constable
added means extra
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A constable brings in an additional standard for a high-security unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded room in an asylum is a secure place to hold a patient, described ironically as accommodation.

clue.text: Girl in a state? Not half

indicators.note: half of the state name is not there, its second four letters removed

parts.note: Delaware is a US state

explanation.surface: A girl in a nervous condition, only half there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; DELAWARE loses its last half to leave DELA.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Adela is a woman's given name, and crosswords often define such names simply as a girl.

clue.text: Record it, capturing revolutionary's shame?

indicators.note: the record and it words capture, or enclose, the revolutionary

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a red is a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: A record that has seized a revolutionary brings disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Discredit is a loss of reputation, so it is a synonym of shame or disgrace.

clue.text: Fingerprints possible to produce, using this?

definitions.text: Fingerprints possible to produce, using this?

parts.words: Fingerprints possible to produce, using this?
parts.note: digits are fingers, so a device whose name hints at fingers and which makes prints

explanation.surface: Forensic equipment for taking fingerprints.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern electronic camera produces prints, and digital puns on digits, or fingers.

clue.text: Rather mischievous rock'n'roll singer sounding drunk?

indicators.note: a drunk slurs the final S into SH

parts.note: Elvis Presley, the king of rock'n'roll

explanation.surface: A singer slurring his words seems a little impish.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvish means like an elf, hence impish or rather mischievous.

clue.text: One shirking work maybe put foot in it

definitions.meaning: a slip-on shoe, something one puts a foot in

explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is an idler, and also a casual slip-on shoe.

clue.text: Managed to occupy holiday cottage made of stone

indicators.note: one piece occupies, or sits inside, the cottage word

parts.note: a gite is a French holiday cottage
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone managed to rent a stone-built holiday cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock, a kind of building stone.

clue.text: Angry about new Conservative team showing no regard for others

indicators.note: the angry word goes about, or around, the rest

parts.note: irate means angry
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Anger at a new Tory team that ignores everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate means thoughtless of other people's feelings.

clue.text: Travel in southern Spain by way of Spanish town

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (Espana)
to go is to travel
via means by way of

explanation.surface: Instructions for journeying through the south of Spain to reach a particular town.
explanation.definitionFit: Segovia is a historic town in central Spain, famous for its Roman aqueduct.

clue.text: Punish child bearing a piece of furniture

parts.note: to cane is to punish by beating with a stick
a person's air is their bearing or demeanour

explanation.surface: A child is punished while carrying an item of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat woven from rattan or cane is a familiar item of furniture.

clue.text: Try the asparagus soup this evening for starters

indicators.note: the starters of the words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A menu suggestion: sample the asparagus soup tonight as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to try a little of it.

clue.text: Film stars failing to shine in English oldies? Wrong

parts.note: mat (or matt) describes a dull, non-glossy finish

indicators.note: the word oldies is put wrong, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Movie stars who no longer sparkle in old English films are judged mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to shine' is matt, here spelt with one T, describing a dull finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Matinee idols are handsome actors adored by cinema audiences, i.e. film stars.

clue.text: Dine out on hot food served up in the city

indicators.note: out in the sense of not in order or broken, so the letters of dine are rearranged
in a down clue served up means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Eating out on hot food served in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINE to EDIN; 'served up' turns H + GRUB into BURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland.

clue.text: Precisely indicate reason for having one form of ID?

definitions.text: reason for having one form of ID?
definitions.meaning: the point, or purpose, of a personal identification number

explanation.definitionFit: To pinpoint is to identify precisely; the PIN point is the purpose of a PIN.

clue.text: Author finally in league with editor, still to go to press?

indicators.note: the last letter goes in the league word

parts.note: a union is a league or alliance

indicators.note: the last letter of the author word

explanation.surface: An author teams up with an editor on a book not yet printed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a printing press; it is the iron used on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are unironed are still waiting to be pressed.

clue.text: Carrying out service right in car depot

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car

indicators.note: the right abbreviation goes in the car and depot words

parts.note: a station is a depot, as in a bus station

explanation.surface: Doing a service on a car at the garage depot is the right thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ministration is the act of giving help or service, so carrying out service fits.

clue.text: Sound of laughter about North Carolina's governor

indicators.note: the laughter goes about, or around, the state abbreviation

parts.note: ho-ho is a laughing sound
NC is the abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: Laughter surrounds the governor of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A honcho is slang for the boss or person in charge, one who governs.

clue.text: Repeat the usual rubbish

parts.note: par is the normal or usual level
rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Trotting out the same old nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, as the bird does.

clue.text: Brave old man of wisdom

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A courageous elderly man full of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Osage are a Native American people.

clue.text: One getting a constant buzz out of working in the colony?

definitions.text: One getting a constant buzz out of working in the colony?

parts.words: One getting a constant buzz out of working in the colony?
parts.note: reads like a keen worker in an overseas settlement, but the buzz is literal and the colony is one of insects in a hive

explanation.surface: Someone who gets endless excitement from working in a colonial outpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends hives is surrounded by the buzzing of a bee colony.

clue.text: Female from Belize was eliminating extremists

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters, the extremes

explanation.surface: A woman from Belize used to remove radicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza is a girl's name, so it stands for a female.

clue.text: Seafarer pushed back Iberia's rocky limits

indicators.note: the run of letters is pushed back, so read from right to left
the letters lie within the limits of the words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A sailor was driven back by the rocky coast of Iberia.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Iberia's rocky' backwards and the run sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a pirate, a kind of seafarer, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Foreign man shelters queen

indicators.note: the man word shelters, or holds inside it, the queen word

parts.note: Ian is a man's name
a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: A man protects a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Iranian means from Iran, so to a British solver it is one example of foreign.

clue.text: High tech phone — answer received with minimal cost

indicators.note: the answer abbreviation is received into the rearranged letters
high in the sense of intoxicated, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: An advanced telephone that came cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' rearranges TECH and PHONE, and 'received' takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the cheap means doing it for as little money as possible.

clue.text: Male pin-up taking year off work at university

indicators.note: the year abbreviation comes off the word for academic work

parts.note: to study is to work at university

explanation.surface: A handsome poster boy takes a gap year from his degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... off' is the deletion indicator, with 'taking' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a sexually attractive man, the sort put up as a pin-up.
